newsitem.title: MALAWI: CLASHES AS MALAWI CIVIL SERVANTS STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: CLASHES AS MALAWI CIVIL SERVANTS STRIKE.

text.p: Striking Malawi civil servants stoned ministers' cars outside parliament in Zomba on Monday, parliamentary sources said.

Civil servants walked out on Monday to push for a 100 percent wage rise recommended by an independent commission of inquiry after the government last week awarded only an average 24 percent instead of the recommended 100 percent.
Parliamentary officials told Reuters they had joined the strike but had not joined in the clashes.
"We are sitting in our offices making personal calls," one source said and added that it was unclear how widespread the strike was.
Civil servants' union leader Thomas Banda last week threatened the entire 100,000 strong civil service would strike if the government did not pay more.
Government said it had declined to award the 100 percent increase for fear of destablising the country's economy which in 1996 grew by more than nine percent.
Official projections forecast economic growth of seven percent in 1997 with the chiefly agriculture-based economy boosted by recent good rains.

Official figures show annual inflation for last December dropped to 6.7 percent from as high as 98 percent in December 1995. But analysts said ordinary citizens in the roughly 10 million population were still feeling the effects of previous high inflation.

Sources in the country's commercial city Blantyre said strikers assembled at the government regional office early Monday morning to be addressed by Banda and organise demonstrations due to begin on Tuesday.
World Bank representative Arif Zulfiqar said the government needed to halve its civil service to be able to award a 100 percent pay rise.
Government said it would award senior civil servants 10 percent and the lowest-paid servants 47 percent.
